title: A Scan Taken While Moving: Every Beam Is Fired From a Different Place, and the Wall That Bends in the Point Cloud Is the Vehicle's Own Motion

questions.question: Why is a scan not a photograph?
options: The beams are fired one after another, and the sensor moves between them
questions.explanation: A sweep takes 0.1 s, and the first and last beams are fired from different places if the vehicle moves. A photograph is taken at one instant.

questions.question: A turn of 1 rad/s over a sweep of 0.1 s turned the sensor:
questions.explanation: One radian a second for a tenth of a second is 0.1 rad, which is 5.7 degrees. The last beam is aimed that far from where the cloud assumes.

questions.question: A wall straight ahead read 0.119 m from straight. After deskewing:
questions.explanation: Each beam's point is placed with the pose its beam was fired from and then put in the frame of the start of the sweep. The wall came out straight.

questions.question: At 5 m/s a sweep of 0.1 s skews the cloud by:
questions.explanation: Speed times the sweep time. At walking pace it hardly shows; at 5 m/s it is half a metre from one side of the cloud to the other.

questions.question: Why do the far points move most in a turn?
options: They are fired later in the sweep
A point moves by range times turn rate times time
questions.explanation: A turn swings every point through the same angle, and a point's shift is that angle times its range: 2.00 m at 20 m for 1 rad/s.

questions.question: Why must the two poses of the sweep come from something fast?
options: A localiser at 1 Hz cannot give the pose at the start and end of 0.1 s
They are only needed to a metre
questions.explanation: The correction needs the pose at both ends of a tenth of a second. Only wheel odometry or an inertial sensor reports that often.
